newsitem.title: USA: FDA proposes tighter ruminant-to-ruminant feed ban.
newsitem.headline: FDA proposes tighter ruminant-to-ruminant feed ban.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposed Wednesday tighter restrictions on the use of rendered carcasses in livestock feed.

Under the proposed rule put on display at the Government Printing Office, the ruminant-to-ruminant feed ban would be expanded to include all mammalian protein with some exceptions, including tissue from hogs.
By banning mammalian protein, FDA would extend the ban to tissue from cats, dogs and horses, in addition to cattle and sheep already covered, a spokesman said.
The proposed rule was expected to appear in Thursday's issue of the Federal Register. FDA set a 10-day comment period, closing April 28.
FDA has spent months developing the ruminant-to-ruminant feed ban as a line of defense to prevent a U.S. occurence of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), known as mad cow disease.
Pork was exempted because no transmissible spongiform encephalopathy has been associated with swine, FDA said.
